statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and no NQ price path exists to score, while Stress steps up to 64 as the Saudi-Houthi exchange broadened on Saturday with an unclaimed fire at Aramco's Riyadh refinery, Houthi-affiliated claims of 26 Saudi air strikes on Sanaa, and a declared naval blockade on Saudi Red Sea shipping.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band for every hour of this window, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON and green throughout. All 24 scored hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt; the restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies about four hours beyond the final scored hour, so restart gap risk is not scored in this publication. The Gulf equity session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October is the only interval containing an open venue able to respond to the refinery incident, and under the delayed-evidence rule it informs Stress and Confidence rather than current Nasdaq-100 structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this publication.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 while a broadened Saudi-Houthi exchange and an unclaimed Riyadh refinery fire lift Stress to 64
body: Friday 2 October remains the last traded session before the halt, and its verified levels are unchanged: the Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, with a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range. The structurally decisive detail for this framework is that the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced into a close near the session low. That is orderly mean reversion, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3 across the whole window. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 with a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt. The soft September employment report behind that close showed unemployment ticking up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings up only 0.1% on the month, yet Treasury yields reversed upward anyway: the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%, with Friday's close reported at 4.84% and 5.28% and an intraday 10-year high described as the strongest since 2002. That conflict between a soft labour print and a higher curve is a Stress and Confidence input, not a Tail input. Brent settled at $102.25, down 0.06% on the day but up 7.05% on the month and 58.45% on the year. The material change since the previous publication is that the Yemen thread broadened from a single unexplained incident into a reported bilateral military exchange. Reuters-sourced reporting describes a plume of smoke and flames near Aramco's Riyadh refinery from Saturday morning, with the cause not immediately clear; as of this assessment neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco had confirmed the incident, its cause, any damage, casualties or production impact, and no group had claimed responsibility. Separately, France 24 reports the Houthi-affiliated channel Al-Masirah alleging that Saudi aircraft struck Sanaa 26 times on Saturday, which Riyadh has not confirmed, alongside a Saudi-led coalition account of intercepting two ballistic missiles and four drones aimed at Khamis Mushait and Jazan, and a Houthi-declared naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea. Reuters reporting carried by the Jerusalem Post describes Saudi Arabia preparing an operation to retake the Bab al-Mandeb strait, led by Yemeni ground forces under Saudi air support and potentially mobilising more than 100,000 troops, with timing estimates spanning from within a week to after the U.S. midterm elections and Washington providing advisers and intelligence but declining air strikes. Stress therefore steps up to 64 from 60 and drifts to 73 across the window. Tail does not follow, because this framework requires an observed pathological price path rather than an unresolved mechanism: with every venue relevant to the Nasdaq-100 closed, the escalation produces restart gap risk, not persistent one-way structure. The 2026 precedent supports that separation, since earlier strikes on Aramco facilities produced temporary interruptions the company described as immaterial to operations and equity markets absorbed them without a no-retracement path. Confidence is 83: the index level, session range and close, volatility, the H.15 curve, Brent and the seven-day U.S. calendar were each verified from primary or authoritative current sources this run, and the open items are the unexplained Riyadh fire, the absence of any Saudi statement, and a disputed strike count, with one outlet headlining 56 strikes against the 26 that France 24 attributes to Al-Masirah. The shared Finviz context file carried a generatedAt of 29 September and a partial collection status, leaving it more than four days stale, so it was discarded and this assessment rests entirely on independent research. No Nasdaq-100 futures or CFD price discovery is available anywhere inside this forecast window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. The window opens in Friday's post-payroll U.S. session with Tail 21-22 and Stress 76-78 under a mixed mode, then decays steadily after the 21:00Z futures close: Tail falls from 14 to 3 and Stress from 74 to 52 across the overnight and Saturday hours, with the mode settling to normal from 00:00Z. The last seven hours sit flat at Tail 3 while Stress troughs at 52 and recovers to 60 as the Gulf escalation thread reopened and broadened.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this forecast window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no NQ price path can form; Tail is held at 3 and ticks only to 5 late, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 64 to 73 because the broadened Saudi-Houthi exchange, the unclaimed Riyadh refinery fire, the declared Red Sea blockade and a 5.28% 10-year accumulate with no venue able to price them. Confidence eases from 83 to 77 as Friday's verified levels age, lifting briefly to 80 during the Gulf session. That Gulf equity session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z on 4 October is the one genuinely differentiating interval and the only open market relevant to the refinery incident; under the delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure. The CME restart at 22:00Z on 4 October lies about four hours past the final scored hour, so the first genuine post-weekend price-path evidence, and any restart gap, fall outside this horizon.
